To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IT steering committee-driven governance initiatives are positively related to IT-related capabilities, which in turn are positively related to internal process level performance, customer service and firm level performance.
IT steering committees are effective in building firm’s IT-related management and IT infrastructure capabilities, which in turn improves firm’s internal processes and firm-level outcomes.

IT steering committee-driven governance initiatives positively relate with the level of a firm’s IT-related capability, which in turn, improves the firm’s internal processes, customer services and firm-level performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how firms should manage the acquisition and use of technology to improve their business processes and firm performance.
the role of the IT steering committee in improving the effectiveness of IT governance.
the effectiveness of IT governance in building performance-differenting IT-related capabilities, and how these capabilities are related to performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effectiveness of IT governance initiatives is positively related to IT-related capabilities, and that IT-related capabilities are positively related to firm-level performance.
the effectiveness of IT governance initiatives is positively associated to a firms’ IT-related capabilities.
IT governance is a process, and the process should be managed by the firm’s IT governance steering committee.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more effective IT governance is, the more likely it would be able to generate IT-related capabilities.
IT-related capabilities are the key to effective IT governance.
IT governance is a process of building and sustaining a firm’s IT-related capability, which would ultimately contribute to its business process improvement and firm-level performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
firms need to invest in IT governance initiatives that would improve their IT-related capabilities to achieve performance-differentiating outcomes.
firms need to ensure that they have a clear understanding of the capabilities they want to develop through their IT governance initiatives.

the success of IT governance initiatives is not only dependent on the effectiveness of IT governance arrangements, but also on the extent to which the initiatives build IT-related capabilities that are critical for the firm’s success.
